deviations: Partition scope: the spec lists five partitions (ops_overview/settlement_coverage/cash_bridge/fee_pairing/identity_access); the contract/revenue/bank-balance reads are aggregated indirectly through the PH-291 ops_overview partition (which already contains contract/settlement/revenue/time/onboarding/cash sections) rather than duplicated as a second owner, per the spec's 'no second owner' constraint.

PM access: pm sees managed-project summaries for ops_overview/settlement_coverage/fee_pairing/identity_access because those read services scope rows to visible managed projects; the cash_bridge partition is marked available=false with missing=['permission'] for pm because bank/cash facts carry no project attribution (same limitation disclosed by PH-279/PH-288), rather than leaking company-wide cash.

Missing semantics: partitions return issue_count=None + missing codes (e.g. permission, import_preview_persistence_not_implemented from PH-291) instead of substituting 0, matching the spec's null+missing requirement.
The workbench performs no generic audit and no receipt/session persistence; the read path is side-effect free and does not change verify_integrity.
No export is implemented here (PH-304 owns CSV export); the workbench only links to the existing read pages via drill URLs.
Counterexamples/tests never UPDATE/DELETE historical rows; the workbench itself is read-only, so append-only triggers are untouched.

Single worker owns the whole write set (delivery workbench service/view/form/domain metadata/template, delivery urls, two test files, governance); no parallel slice writes these files; independent review is pending.
